script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for January 30. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Look at your hand.  Every atom in it will be replaced over the next several years.  The cells in your stomach lining?

Your body replaces billions of cells daily. Your skeleton is completely renewed every 10 years. Your taste buds last about 2 weeks. The 'you' from 7 years ago shares almost no physical matter with the you today. You are continuity without permanence. 2,500 years ago, Heraclitus said: 'You cannot step into the same river twice—for it is not the same river, and you are not the same person. ' Ancient wisdom that modern physics confirms.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Fighting change is fighting reality.  The art of living is learning to flow with impermanence—to hold things lightly, love fully, and release gracefully.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Impermanence Practice - Letting Go.

Here's your activity: Think of something you're holding onto that's already changing or gone—a relationship, a phase of life, an old version of yourself. Write a short letter saying goodbye to it. Thank it for what it gave you. Then, symbolically release it. This helps you practice acceptance of change through reflection.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why everything changes can be applied to impermanence practice - letting go. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
